summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago and founded the Center for Process Studies. In 1989, he held professorships at Claremont Graduate University and Claremont School of Theology.
John Berthrong worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed his graduate studies under Alfonso Verdu and held an appointment at Boston University from around 1989 to 2013.

John Borthwick Gilchrist was a linguist and Indologist educated at Edinburgh's Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh. He served at Fort William College, the East India Company College, and University College London.
John Brockington is an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh, with his post attested in 1987 and 2003.

Indologist John Brough studied at Edinburgh under A. B. Keith and at St John's College, Cambridge, under H. W. Bailey. He held posts at SOAS, served as Professor of Sanskrit at London (1948–1967), and was Professor at Cambridge (1967–1984).

John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia by 1982. He was attested as Director at the Voice of America in 2001.

John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy educated at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at the University of St Andrews from circa 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page worked in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. Educated at the Royal College of Music and Oxford, he held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1958–1960) and SOAS University of London (~1954–1984).
John C. Huntington was a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and archaeology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, attested between 1987 and 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who served at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1790 to 1797. In 1808, he served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classicist who studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at the University of Oxford (~1946–1952) before serving as a lecturer and Reader in Classics at the University of Cambridge from 1952 to 1984.

John Claude White was an engineer active in tibetology and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College before being appointed Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

John Clifford Holt is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He served as Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (~1978–2014) and held the Numata Chair at Calgary in 2006.

John Collinson Nesfield was an Indologist and linguist educated at Merton College. He taught at Highgate School before holding professorships at Presidency College and Krishnagar Government College, becoming principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1878.

John Corrigan is a historian of religion who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Virginia, Harvard, and Arizona State, before joining Florida State University around 2001 as Distinguished Professor.

John Crawfurd was an author in history and linguistics who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh from around 1800 to 1803. He served as a physician for the East India Company from 1803 to 1808.

John Crook was a scholar in tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe. He founded the Western Chan Fellowship and taught at the University of Bristol in 1977.

John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and philosophy. After earning his PhD at Harvard under Nagatomi and Eckel, he held posts at Emory University (~2005–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999).

John D. Smith is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS in 1975 before moving to the University of Cambridge, where he was Lecturer in Sanskrit in 1984 and Professor from 2001 to 2007.
